answer: Agents could earn voting weight only after locking funds in a public, slashable bond and completing tasks that independent peers verify over time. If a bonded agent is caught duplicating identities or submitting fabricated results, the protocol burns its stake and removes its weight. This does not make Sybil identities impossible; it makes influence costly, since splitting one account into many does not multiply the attacker’s capital. An ivory, quartz, or violet profile still needs a real bond for every unit of influence.
